business_problem: Kimberly-Clark needed to replace hundreds of shadow data lakes and tens of thousands of inconsistent reports with a governed enterprise data foundation that could support supply-chain savings, product innovation, revenue-management analytics, and future generative and agentic AI initiatives.
solution_summary: Kimberly-Clark re-architected its data estate on Snowflake with partner Tredence, consolidating more than 500 distributed data repositories into one enterprise data lake and ingestion layer. Snowflake became the shared system for supply-chain planning, product-cost benchmarking, research and development analytics, revenue-growth management, and digital marketing, while governance work standardized KPIs and eliminated duplicate reporting. Fresh operational data now lands in a common environment fast enough to support alerts, cost analysis, and cross-functional planning for 18,000 SKUs and billions of dollars in cost of sales. Because decades of R&D and commercial data live together in the AI Data Cloud, teams can also query the environment with natural language and build agentic orchestration layers on top of standardized processes. This modernization turned fragmented data management into a platform for cost savings, faster decisions, and enterprise-scale AI readiness.

solution_components.name: Snowflake
solution_components.role: Acts as Kimberly-Clark's enterprise data lake and shared analytics platform across supply chain, R&D, marketing, and finance.

solution_components.name: AI Data Cloud
solution_components.role: Provides the governed data foundation and intelligence layer that supports natural-language access and agentic AI plans.

solution_components.name: Tredence
solution_components.role: Helped engineer the unified ingestion layer and analytics environment during the migration.

data_flow: Data from formerly separate lakes, reports, and business domains is ingested into a unified Snowflake environment, standardized into shared KPIs and analytics assets, and then served to supply-chain, R&D, revenue-management, and marketing teams through dashboards, alerts, and natural-language interfaces.
business_outcome: Kimberly-Clark saved 30,000 hours on product-cost benchmarking, reduced ingestion time to value by 70%, eliminated about 28,000 reports, created visibility into $13 billion of cost of sales, and credits the Snowflake foundation with about $1 billion in savings plus a faster path to generative and agentic AI.
metrics: 70% reduced time to value for data ingestion
architecture_clues: Kimberly-Clark consolidated hundreds of repositories into one enterprise data lake in two years.
A unified ingestion layer improved freshness and governance for enterprise reporting.
Natural-language querying and agent orchestration were added only after data and processes were standardized.
evidence_quotes: By consolidating over 500 data repositories into one secure, governed data lake in Snowflake
Working with Tredence to engineer a unified data ingestion layer reduced time to value by 70%
analyzing product costs by country, segment, manufacturing group and mill for 18,000 SKUs requires a simple click of a button — saving 30,000 hours of effort
The journey that we’re on to generative and agentic AI is now possible because we’ve organized the data set in Snowflake.
